en.name: Pier Giorgio Frassati
en.summary: Italian university student and avid mountain climber whose energetic, joyful faith and secret charity to the poor made him a model for young Catholics.
en.body: Pier Giorgio Frassati was the son of a wealthy and largely secular Italian newspaper-owning family, a lively university student passionate about mountaineering, skiing, and social life, who combined this exuberant ordinary youthfulness with a deeply committed personal faith and an extensive, mostly secret ministry to Turin's poor, regularly using his own allowance and spending long hours visiting the sick and needy in the city's poorest neighborhoods, activities his own family only fully discovered after his death. He was also politically active against the rising Fascist movement in Italy, participating in Catholic student organizing at real personal risk. He contracted polio, likely from his contact with the sick he served, and died suddenly in 1925 at only twenty-four; his funeral drew an enormous unexpected crowd of the city's poor whom his family had never known he assisted. His combination of ordinary youthful vigor and hidden holiness made him a natural patron for young Catholics, and he was canonized by Pope Leo XIV in 2025 alongside Carlo Acutis.
